Description: Generate a chemical formula from a SMILES string using RDKit.

Shielding suggests ortho to electron-donating group (e.g., alkyl, alkoxy, amino). So substituents likely carbonyl (EWG) and alkyl/alkoxy (EDG). The alkyl chain is CH2-CH2- attached to benzene? That would be phenethyl group, which is weakly donating. But chemical shift difference seems large. Maybe the donating group is methoxy (OCH3) which strongly donates. Then aromatic protons ortho to methoxy are shielded (~6.8 ppm), ortho to carbonyl deshielded (~7.9 ppm). That matches: 7.17 ppm ortho to methoxy? Actually ortho to methoxy should be more shielded (~6.8). 7.17 is slightly shielded. 7.93 ortho to carbonyl. So likely para-methoxybenzaldehyde derivative? But we have nitrogen.
